messages:
Miguel Rivera: Acme prod reporting p99 jump to ~1200ms (was ~350ms). Started ~2024-10-12 07:20 UTC, plus a handful of 503s. Ticket #8143.
Amy Chen: @miguel thanks — can you paste the deployment id, model variant, and any recent rollouts? also any request ids for 503s?
Miguel Rivera: deployment dv-12-prod, model redwood/gpt-3-large-quant. We rolled a canary at 07:10 (small perf flags) and removed it at 07:18 when alerts fired. Example request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Logs attached to ticket.
Amy Chen: ok. did the canary change quantization / kernel flags?
Miguel Rivera: canary toggled "kv_prefetch=on" and a reduced allocator slab threshold (to try to reduce latency). Don't think it changed model weights.
Kevin Liu: seeing high GPU memory fragmentation on node gpu-3. kv_cache bytes for tenant acme jumped ~3x over last 2 hours. slab_free pages low, allocator churn up. This would increase token latency and cause occasional 503s when OOM fallback triggers.
Maya Oncall: repro steps (minimal):
```bash
# run 30 concurrent chat requests with same convo prefix to warm KV
for i in {1..30}; do \
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-3-large-quant","input":"translate this...","stream":false}' \
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
This reproduces p99 spike locally against the dv-12-prod routing table.
Amy Chen: suggested mitigations (start with low-risk):
- enable aggressive KV TTL for tenant (set 30m) to evict long-lived caches
- lower max_batch_tokens to 256 and max_batch_size to 8 for dv-12-prod
- enable per-tenant eviction heuristics (temporary)
If that stabilizes p99, plan: rolling allocator restart for gpu-3 and a controlled canary revert.
Kevin Liu: collecting diagnostics — run on node:
```bash
# alloc stats
curl http://node-gpu-3:1234/debug/alloc-stats | jq .
# kv sizes
curl http://node-gpu-3:1234/debug/kv-stats | head -n 50
# recent OOM lines
journalctl -u inference-runtime -n 200 | grep -i oom
```
Also capture a small heap snapshot before any restart: `/debug/heap-snapshot?pid=$PID`
SRE Bot: :rotating_light: Alert created INC-2024-8143 — p99 latency > 1s for dv-12-prod, GPU mem frag suspected. Pager notified.
Miguel Rivera: applied KV TTL=30m and lowered batch size at 07:42 UTC. After ~7m p99 dropped to ~480ms, p95 ~120ms. Still seeing ~1-2x/day OOMs with 503s.
Amy Chen: good signal. next safe step: schedule rolling restart of allocator on gpu-3 (non-disruptive if we drain properly). Notify customer of planned mitigation window. We'll keep canary reverted until we confirm allocator behaviour.
Kevin Liu: plan for rolling restart: drain traffic from gpu-3 node -> snapshot heap -> restart allocator (service restart) -> verify alloc-stats and kv-stats -> rejoin. Target 08:15 UTC for first window, staggered 5 min for safety. I'll run a canary on node gpu-5 first.
Maya Oncall: I'll watch metrics and collect p99 heatmap and tail traces during the window. If OOMs persist after allocator restart, escalate to infra for allocator parameter tuning (increase slab compaction aggressiveness / bump small object pool).
Miguel Rivera: customer updated: we told them we're applying TTL + batching throttle; saw immediate improvement; scheduled maintenance 08:15 UTC. They accepted.
Amy Chen: nice. capture the before/after metrics for the postmortem and add concrete repro commands + exact alloc-stats dumps to ticket #8143. We'll also open a follow-up to consider longer-term fixes: per-tenant KV quotas, allocator defrag hooks, and safer canary rollout checks.
Support Bot: note added to ticket #8143: KV TTL applied, batch throttles applied, rolling allocator restart scheduled.
Kevin Liu: one-liner checklist for runbook update:
- add a quick kv-ttl toggle in support console
- add "drain-and-restart-allocator" playbook with exact commands
- add smoke test that runs the minimal repro after restarts
Amy Chen: perfect. I'll own the postmortem. Thanks team :rocket:
